label: <DEL> step of length-9 sequences (plus copy-phase o/r inputs), sparse
explanation: Never fires in the original phase. About 66% of activation mass is on the <DEL> step, nearly all in long sequences (L=9 gives 88% of mass, L=8 10%, never for L<=5); the strongest activations are all at <DEL> with L=9. The rest is in the copy phase, mostly when the input is o (or r), with some extra at the last outputs of L=9 sequences. It is very sparse: only about 10% of L=9 <DEL> steps fire and only about 2.5% of copy-phase o inputs, and I could not find which content decides this (first token and previous token give only weak lift). So the predicate gets high mass recall but very low precision.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: l, 1, p, q, 2, a; least: e, u, w, v) and the current input token, by step (t=11: o, r, g; t=12: o, r, 2, e; t=17: o, r, 2, z); timing cues that raise it most: L=9, L=9 & t=9, L=8 & t=8.
